newsitem.title: USA: NASD expels Stratton Oakmont, principals barred.
newsitem.headline: NASD expels Stratton Oakmont, principals barred.

text.p: NASD Regulation Inc said Thursday it premanently expelled Stratton Oakmont Inc, a New York-based brokerage from the securities industry because of "willful disregard" for regulations.
NASD said it also barred Stratton's president Daniel Porush and head trader Steven Sanders.
The order was issued by the NASDR's National Business Conduct Committee after Stratton Oakmont filed an appeal of an April 1996 decision by the self-regulatory's organization.
The national committee raised the sanction against the brokerage firm to expulsion from the New York panel's penalty of only a one year ban in retail transactions.
The group also increased Sanders' original penalty to a permanent bar from a one-year suspension and affirmed a permanent bar for Porush.

Porush was also fined $250,000 and censured, while Sanders was fined $25,000 and censured, NASD said. Stratton Oakmont was ordered by the committee to pay $416,528 in restitution to customers, fined $500,000 and censured.
The 23-page decision said the bars were necessary because Porush and Sanders "continue to deny responsibility and exhibit no remorse for (their) misconduct.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and a number of state securities regulators around the United States have also sanctioned Stratton Oakmont.
